Harties promises and Hollywood lies

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Imagine you dreamed your child might be the next Charlize Theron, and a casting agency promised they could make it happen once you'd forked out some cash, only to find out you been sold pie in the sky

Unique Selling Point:
From appearing on the Ellen de Generes show to a role in the latest Fast and Furious movie, thats exactly what Bennie Wolmarans, owner of Active Casting Talent Management from Hartebeespoort Dam promises his prospective clients. But once parents and would be actors have paid to sign up to the agency, and paid some more to attend acting workshops Wolmarans hosts, none of the promises ever materialise...

Summary:
Whats more, he's left a group of well known and talented South African artists in the Film, Television and Music industries fuming after not paying them for the work they did at his Acting Workshops. Meanwhile, he's marketing his next round of workshops set to take place in March this year using those same artists names to promote his business, even though most of them will not be participating since he still owes them money from last year's workshops.

Although the monetary amounts involved in this story are relatively small, most parents have spent about R12 000 getting there children registered etc, there are very sexy elements like the following:

1. Well known Afrikaans actor Vaughn Lucas, who stars in the DSTV drama series Getroud met Rugby, is owed money for presenting at Wolmarans's workshops last year. He also made big promises of roles in international films etc which never materialised. He's using Lucas' name to market the next round of workshops, although he won't participate since he's still owed money.

2. We have voice notes sent to Diane du Toit, a mother from Ellisras, who paid for both her children to attend the workshops in 2020 and drove the 3 hour drive from Ellisras to Jhb every saturday for a month so that they could participate. In the voice notes Wolmarans promises that her son Jade will be getting a role in the new Fast and Furious film that is being shot in South Africa (This is all lies, the latest film, Fast 9 is already in post and will be released in 2022). In the voice note Wolmarans claims he's scouting locations in Magaliesburg with both the director and producer of the movie, that they've already bought two helicopters for the production, that he will need to organise accommodation for between 500 to 800 crew... We also have a written whatsapp message where he tells Diane that she and her son Jade will be appearing on the Ellen De Generes show in June of this year.



Further information:
3. Reno Gericke, from a relatively unknown band called BAND1925, who are trying to break into the SA market, took to social media to expose Wolmarans as a fraud and liar after the band were booked for gigs they performed at but never got paid for. They were also promised an audience of between 1000 and 2000 people for a live stream performance and that the technical crew would all be paid for. The live stream was a dismal failure, and the crew have not been paid. They were also sent to do a marketing photo shoot with well known photographer Nelus Engelbrecht from Photo Lounge, which Wolmarans said he would paid for. But months later Nelus was still asking the band when he would be paid, and they eventually had to pay him themselves.

4. Lorna Greyling, an actor who attended the New York Film Academy and hosted the first round of workshops, has not been paid in full for her work last year, and her name is also being used to market the next round of workshops.

5. A photographer, Malise de Meillon, who shot portraits, bio pics etc at the first round of workshops has not been paid.

6. Most real talent agencies and talent managers do not charge joining fees, there are sometimes small registration costs, which come off the first job they book you for. But Wolmarans charges joining fees.

While its not the biggest scam out there, Bennie Wolmarans is taking advantage of both artists currently struggling to make ends meet during the Covid-19 pandemic, as well as unsuspecting parents who have no knowledge of how the industry actually works.



I have confirmed interviews with:

Vaughn Lucas - Getroud Met Rugby star who presented at workshops but was not paid in full.
Lorna Greyling - Actress who also presented and was not paid in full.
Diane Du Toit - Single mother from Ellisras who was promised her son would be starring in Fast and Furious and be featured on Ellen.
Malise de Meillon - Photographer hired to film at workshops who was not paid anything

We have voice note and whatsapp message proof of promises made

Script:


Harties Promises, Hollywood Lies
2nd Draft Script
12 Jan 2021

Voice
Lights, camera, action! For many the dream is to star in mega budget Hollywood productions. Whether you’re a big name star or just getting started, being represented by a talent agent could mean the difference between success or failure.

Link Derek
Taylor Swift, Queen, the Beatles, Jimi Hendrix, even the king himself Elvis Presley all fell foul to managers who promised the world and failed to deliver. But it’s not only the legends who get ripped off.

Voice
In November last year, Heidi Nel sent her two children to acting workshops organised by this man, Bennie Wolmarans, and his company Active Casting Talent Management.

Sound Up Heidi
My daughter’s name is Alicia, she’s 16, and Marko is 11, and they love acting.

Voice
She says the workshops went off without a hitch.

Sound Up Heidi
Derek: Did Alicia and Marko enjoy these workshops?

Heidi: Oh they loved it, they enjoyed every bit of it.

Voice
But she says - two months later, Bennie still owes her for goods she paid for as part of the workshops.

Sound Up Heidi
Well we got invoices which we paid for, photo shoots, makeup, portfolios etc. And nothing of that has happened.

Voice
Single mother Diane du Toit from Lephalale says she’s struggling to make ends meet, especially in the current Covid pandemic. But like any loving parent , she made a plan to pay for her son Jade to attend last years workshops.

Sound Up Diane
He told us that he would give Jade a role in the Fast and the Furious that was being shot in Magaliesburg in December.

Voice
This is an extract from one of two voice notes Wolmarans sent du Toit last year.

Sound Up Bennie Wolmarans Voice Note (Translated from Afrikaans)
Hi good evening Diane, hope you are doing well. Yes I was with one of the producers and the director of the new international film that will start now in the second week of December.I think we can possibly also see if we can get Jade a role in this film. It is the new Fast and the Furious that we are going to produce here in South Africa.






Voice
According to the international database IMDb, the latest instalment in the popular franchise has in fact already completed production, and was filmed in Georgia, Scotland and England. Needless to say, Jade was never cast in the film. Du Toit says Wolmarans likes to namedrop to get parents to buy into his workshops, as can be heard in his second voice note.

Sound Up Bennie Wolmarans Voice Note (Translated from Afrikaans)
We will definitely, i think we will definitely get Jade… Because I think that’s why it’s also important to do the workshop and to attend. And yes it’s really going to be amazing and fantastic. Greetings, Bennie.

Voice
He also wanted to charge du Toit an upfront fee to sign Jade up with Active Casting Talent Management.

Sound Up Diane
then he wants to put him on the books again because he can’t get him work if he doesn’t put him on the books, then it was R1100.

Voice
This man, who is a well known actor, has asked us to hide his identity because he is currently in sensitive negotiations with major international film studios. He says reputable agencies don’t expect artists to pay a joining fee upfront, the fee is usually deducted from the first job you get booked for.

Sound Up
Derek: You work for some of the big agencies, do you ever have to pay upfront for them to represent you?

Man X: My agency has never charged, ever. The plain and simple fact of the matter is that when I went onto their books, my first commission was slightly higher, to cover an admin fee. And when I say slightly higher, I remember the amount exactly, it was a R120.


Voice
Heidi Nel says so far she’s paid Wolmarans nearly R13 000, about R5000 of which was a deposit for a new round of workshops he’s promoting for March this year. She was especially excited about this whatsapp message from Bennie, where he claimed that prolific filmmaker Leon Schuster would also be there.

Sound Up Heidi
He said that there’s going to be short films being done, and Leon Schuster is going to be there and help them and film it.

Voice
We decided to call Schuster to ask him if he would be in attendance, and his response could best be summarised by his iconic line, “oh Schucks”.

Sound Up Leon Schuster
Derek: Leon, apparently you’re presenting acting workhops for Bennie Wolmarans this year, in March?

Leon: Absolutely bull dust! And this enrages me because it’s happened before. Dit maak my de donner in!

Derek: I can see that Leon, but have you heard of Bennie Wolmarans?

Leon: I’ve never heard of Bennie Wolmarans. It’s unfair… They should stand at an intersection naked, with a cardboard saying I am playing the naked beggar in Leon Schuster’s new movie “Oh Schucks Ive Been Scammed”. Jissie dit maak my kwaad hoor.

Voice
Diane du Toit believes that another of his promises is just pie in the sky. In these Facebook posts he claims he will be appearing on the Ellen de Generes show with Hollywood star Mark Wahlberg and two of Wolmarans’ actors - one of which would have been Jade.

Sound Up Diane
He sent me a whatsapp, for the 1st of June, we were going to America, and he had two international films that he was going to shoot there.

Link Derek
It may be a long stretch to compare Hartebeespoort with Hollywood, but as top acting coaches say, take your wallet and run if an agent asks for money to represent you, promises to make you a star if you give them money, or tries to make you take acting classes to become famous. That would be three strikes for Bennie Wolmarans.

Voice
Actress and former Mrs South Africa Lorna Greyling, who studied acting at the world famous New York Film Academy, was hired by Wolmerans to host his acting workshops.

Sound Up Lorna
Derek: And you became the poster girl for his agency?

Lorna: Oh my goodness, yes, I was everywhere. I was on social media, he was phoning various radio stations…

Voice
Initially, Wolmarans booked her to present the workshops for the month of October - so she declined other offers she had.

Sound Up Lorna
From Binnelanders, makeup work that I do, all kinds of things, which I obviously had to decline because I was now booked for the workshops.

Voice
But she says Wolmarans changed the dates of the workshops to November at the last minute. And she claims he still owes her some of the money for presenting his courses.

Sound Up Lorna
My picture is on the poster, so it seems like I’m involved in his agency. But ja, I’m still short about half of the month of november as well as I got no payment for October month.

Voice
Aspiring screenwriter, editor and photographer Malise de Meillon says last year she paid Wolmarans R3500 to represent her.

Sound Up Malise
Malise: He was offering to get me jobs by different studios. Whether it was more behind the scenes stuff, writing, editing, camera work, and possibly even getting into the acting scene.


Voice
But she says he still hasn’t paid her for photography she did at his workshops.

Sound Up Malise
And never saw the payment.

Voice
And after paying to join his agency, she’s never received a contract either.

Sound Up Malise
And ja, I just kept asking him where’s the contract, where do we start, and nothing ever came of it.

Voice
Initially, Bennie Wolmarans did not respond to our emailed request for an interview, so we decided to give him a call.

Sound Up Bennie phonecall
Derek: Hi, is that Bennie Wolmarans?

Bennie: Yes, speaking.

Derek: From Active Casting Talent Management?

PHONE IS PUT DOWN

Derek: That’s it.

Voice
Wolmarans didn’t answer his phone again, but he did start warning artists not to speak to Carte Blanche. In this email, sent to Lorna Greyling, Bennie Wolmarans called her a liar and a snake, and said he would destroy her and her husband’s careers for speaking to the media.

Link Derek
Bennie notified many artists that they were not allowed to discuss anything with third parties, unless his company had been notified. And speaking to Carte Blanche would have legal consequences.

Voice
Cape Town based musicians, brothers Reno, Jeff and David-Lee Gericke, who are known as the 1925Band, were also warned about speaking to the media. Reno says Wolmarans promised them the world but failed to deliver.

Sound Up Reno
He said we’re going to see a thousand to two thousand people joining the Facebook live performance, I think the maximum that we reached was I think 80 people.

Voice
The relationship has since soured, with both sides claiming the other party owes them money, and seeking legal advice.

Link Derek
So we did some digging, and found out that Bennie is renting a garden cottage in Hartebeespoort, and made a plan to put some of the accusations to him in person. But then he replied to our email, threatening that he would summons Carte Blanche, the production company and the journalist, that would be myself, if anything was said or aired about his company without his permission.



Voice
To be fair, we emailed him a detailed list of questions. But since he didn’t answer all of them, we sent our producer and a camera crew to his house.

Sound Up Graham
Hello? Bennie it’s Graham Coetzer from Carte Blanche.
Sound of Voice Mail - You have reached the mailbox of…

Voice
But no one was answering the door, or Bennie’s phone. In his written response, Wolmarans said he told parents that:

- “our Professional Photographer had a backlog of Photo shoots to be done and they are on the Schedule.”

He said he could not respond to our questions about the Fast and Furious because: “I have signed a non disclosure Agreement”

He denied owing actors who presented at his workshops payments, saying: “We don’t owe any actors any money at all.”

He also said that all crew booked at the workshops “have been paid in full”, and that “Everyone has received their contracts”.

He denied allegations that he had promised 1925Band a large online audience, saying: “We have never promised 1925Band anything, they did not pay ACTM for any PR, Marketing services at all”.

And as far as Leon Schuster and Ellen de Generes are concerned? Wolmarans never responded to our questions.
























Promos

Promo 1
Irate parents and unpaid actors, we investigate a casting agent who sold his clients dreams of starring in big budget Hollywood productions, only for them to find out it was all just pie in the sky.

Promo 2
Imagine appearing on the Ellen de Generes show or getting a role in the latest Fast and the Furious film, we investigate a local casting agent’s grandiose promises which have left many artists fuming.

Promo 3
Hollywood talk shows and blockbuster movies, promises one casting agent made to aspiring young actors to attend his acting workshops, only to have their dreams dashed after their parents handed over the cash.

It’s unfair… They should stand at an intersection naked, with a cardboard saying I am playing the naked beggar in Leon Schuster’s new movie “Oh Schucks Ive Been Scammed”. Jissie dit maak my kwaad hoor. Voice Diane du Toit believes that another of his promises is just pie in the sky. In these Facebook posts he claims he will be appearing on the Ellen de Generes show with Hollywood star Mark Wahlberg and two of Wolmarans’ actors - one of which would have been Jade. Sound Up Diane He sent me a whatsapp, for the 1st of June, we were going to America, and he had two international films that he was going to shoot there. Link Derek It may be a long stretch to compare Hartebeespoort with Hollywood, but as top acting coaches say, take your wallet and run if an agent asks for money to represent you, promises to make you a star if you give them money, or tries to make you take acting classes to become famous. That would be three strikes for Bennie Wolmarans. Voice Actress and former Mrs South Africa Lorna Greyling, who studied acting at the world famous New York Film Academy, was hired by Wolmerans to host his acting workshops. Sound Up Lorna Derek: And you became the poster girl for his agency? Lorna: Oh my goodness, yes, I was everywhere. I was on social media, he was phoning various radio stations… Voice Initially, Wolmarans booked her to present the workshops for the month of October - so she declined other offers she had. Sound Up Lorna From Binnelanders, makeup work that I do, all kinds of things, which I obviously had to decline because I was now booked for the workshops. Voice But she says Wolmarans changed the dates of the workshops to November at the last minute. And she claims he still owes her some of the money for presenting his courses. Sound Up Lorna My picture is on the poster, so it seems like I’m involved in his agency. But ja, I’m still short about half of the month of november as well as I got no payment for October month. Voice Aspiring screenwriter, editor and photographer Malise de Meillon says last year she paid Wolmarans R3500 to represent her. Sound Up Malise Malise: He was offering to get me jobs by different studios. Whether it was more behind the scenes stuff, writing, editing, camera work, and possibly even getting into the acting scene. Voice But she says he still hasn’t paid her for photography she did at his workshops. Sound Up Malise And never saw the payment. Voice And after paying to join his agency, she’s never received a contract either. Sound Up Malise And ja, I just kept asking him where’s the contract, where do we start, and nothing ever came of it. Voice Initially, Bennie Wolmarans did not respond to our emailed request for an interview, so we decided to give him a call. Sound Up Bennie phonecall Derek: Hi, is that Bennie Wolmarans? Bennie: Yes, speaking. Derek: From Active Casting Talent Management? PHONE IS PUT DOWN Derek: That’s it. Voice Wolmarans didn’t answer his phone again, but he did start warning artists not to speak to Carte Blanche. In this email, sent to Lorna Greyling, Bennie Wolmarans called her a liar and a snake, and said he would destroy her and her husband’s careers for speaking to the media. Link Derek Bennie notified many artists that they were not allowed to discuss anything with third parties, unless his company had been notified. And speaking to Carte Blanche would have legal consequences. Voice Cape Town based musicians, brothers Reno, Jeff and David-Lee Gericke, who are known as the 1925Band, were also warned about speaking to the media. Reno says Wolmarans promised them the world but failed to deliver. Sound Up Reno He said we’re going to see a thousand to two thousand people joining the Facebook live performance, I think the maximum that we reached was I think 80 people. Voice The relationship has since soured, with both sides claiming the other party owes them money, and seeking legal advice. Link Derek So we did some digging, and found out that Bennie is renting a garden cottage in Hartebeespoort, and made a plan to put some of the accusations to him in person. But then he replied to our email, threatening that he would summons Carte Blanche, the production company and the journalist, that would be myself, if anything was said or aired about his company without his permission. Voice To be fair, we emailed him a detailed list of questions. But since he didn’t answer all of them, we sent our producer and a camera crew to his house. Sound Up Graham Hello? Bennie it’s Graham Coetzer from Carte Blanche. Sound of Voice Mail - You have reached the mailbox of… Voice But no one was answering the door, or Bennie’s phone. In his written response, Wolmarans said he told parents that: - “our Professional Photographer had a backlog of Photo shoots to be done and they are on the Schedule.” He said he could not respond to our questions about the Fast and Furious because: “I have signed a non disclosure Agreement” He denied owing actors who presented at his workshops payments, saying: “We don’t owe any actors any money at all.” He also said that all crew booked at the workshops “have been paid in full”, and that “Everyone has received their contracts”. He denied allegations that he had promised 1925Band a large online audience, saying: “We have never promised 1925Band anything, they did not pay ACTM for any PR, Marketing services at all”. And as far as Leon Schuster and Ellen de Generes are concerned? Wolmarans never responded to our questions. Promos Promo 1 Irate parents and unpaid actors, we investigate a casting agent who sold his clients dreams of starring in big budget Hollywood productions, only for them to find out it was all just pie in the sky. Promo 2 Imagine appearing on the Ellen de Generes show or getting a role in the latest Fast and the Furious film, we investigate a local casting agent’s grandiose promises which have left many artists fuming. Promo 3 Hollywood talk shows and blockbuster movies, promises one casting agent made to aspiring young actors to attend his acting workshops, only to have their dreams dashed after their parents handed over the cash.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Imagine you dreamed your child might be the next Charlize Theron, and a casting agency promised they could make it happen once you'd forked out some cash, only to find out you been sold pie in the sky
metadata.Unique Selling Point: From appearing on the Ellen de Generes show to a role in the latest Fast and Furious movie, thats exactly what Bennie Wolmarans, owner of Active Casting Talent Management from Hartebeespoort Dam promises his prospective clients. But once parents and would be actors have paid to sign up to the agency, and paid some more to attend acting workshops Wolmarans hosts, none of the promises ever materialise...
metadata.Summary: Whats more, he's left a group of well known and talented South African artists in the Film, Television and Music industries fuming after not paying them for the work they did at his Acting Workshops. Meanwhile, he's marketing his next round of workshops set to take place in March this year using those same artists names to promote his business, even though most of them will not be participating since he still owes them money from last year's workshops. Although the monetary amounts involved in this story are relatively small, most parents have spent about R12 000 getting there children registered etc, there are very sexy elements like the following: 1. Well known Afrikaans actor Vaughn Lucas, who stars in the DSTV drama series Getroud met Rugby, is owed money for presenting at Wolmarans's workshops last year. He also made big promises of roles in international films etc which never materialised. He's using Lucas' name to market the next round of workshops, although he won't participate since he's still owed money. 2. We have voice notes sent to Diane du Toit, a mother from Ellisras, who paid for both her children to attend the workshops in 2020 and drove the 3 hour drive from Ellisras to Jhb every saturday for a month so that they could participate. In the voice notes Wolmarans promises that her son Jade will be getting a role in the new Fast and Furious film that is being shot in South Africa (This is all lies, the latest film, Fast 9 is already in post and will be released in 2022). In the voice note Wolmarans claims he's scouting locations in Magaliesburg with both the director and producer of the movie, that they've already bought two helicopters for the production, that he will need to organise accommodation for between 500 to 800 crew... We also have a written whatsapp message where he tells Diane that she and her son Jade will be appearing on the Ellen De Generes show in June of this year.
metadata.Further information: 3. Reno Gericke, from a relatively unknown band called BAND1925, who are trying to break into the SA market, took to social media to expose Wolmarans as a fraud and liar after the band were booked for gigs they performed at but never got paid for. They were also promised an audience of between 1000 and 2000 people for a live stream performance and that the technical crew would all be paid for. The live stream was a dismal failure, and the crew have not been paid. They were also sent to do a marketing photo shoot with well known photographer Nelus Engelbrecht from Photo Lounge, which Wolmarans said he would paid for. But months later Nelus was still asking the band when he would be paid, and they eventually had to pay him themselves. 4. Lorna Greyling, an actor who attended the New York Film Academy and hosted the first round of workshops, has not been paid in full for her work last year, and her name is also being used to market the next round of workshops. 5. A photographer, Malise de Meillon, who shot portraits, bio pics etc at the first round of workshops has not been paid. 6. Most real talent agencies and talent managers do not charge joining fees, there are sometimes small registration costs, which come off the first job they book you for. But Wolmarans charges joining fees. While its not the biggest scam out there, Bennie Wolmarans is taking advantage of both artists currently struggling to make ends meet during the Covid-19 pandemic, as well as unsuspecting parents who have no knowledge of how the industry actually works. I have confirmed interviews with: Vaughn Lucas - Getroud Met Rugby star who presented at workshops but was not paid in full. Lorna Greyling - Actress who also presented and was not paid in full. Diane Du Toit - Single mother from Ellisras who was promised her son would be starring in Fast and Furious and be featured on Ellen. Malise de Meillon - Photographer hired to film at workshops who was not paid anything We have voice note and whatsapp message proof of promises made
